Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates dense, curvilinear calcification outlining the anterior and inferior borders of the heart, specifically along the right ventricular surface and atrioventricular groove. This "eggshell" calcification pattern is pathognomonic for constrictive calcified pericarditis, which aligns with the clinical presentation of a systolic murmur potentially caused by associated valvular or flow abnormalities.
